column1: EarnIn (Activehours)
column5: Colorado AG Weiser + the state UCCC Administrator sued Activehours Inc. d/b/a EarnIn, alleging its direct-to-consumer advances are unlicensed high-cost payday loans under the CO UCCC, the Deferred Deposit Loan Act and the CO Consumer Protection Act. Complaint: 3.1M transactions to CO consumers Jan-2023 to Jul-2025, ~$300M advanced, >$16M collected in tips + expedited-transfer fees, average APR ~388%.
column6: Indirect - second state AG to sue the SAME provider (DC AG preceded it). A repeat-defendant pattern is a different signal from a widening-target pattern: it means the theory of liability is being tested, not just the sector.
column7: CO consumers paid ~$16M in fees on advances the state says were loans; if the classification sticks the product is unavailable or repriced in CO.
column9: Colorado AG press release 2026-08-27; National Law Review; Consumer Finance Monitor 2026-09-08; American Banker (pulled 2026-09-10)
column10: P07 leg - narrow state-AG count now NY+MN+DC+CO = 4 of 5. NOT a failure and must not be counted toward P04: DISTRESS != FAILURE is P04's registered calibration discriminator.

column1: LendingPoint
column5: KBRA DOWNGRADED SIX CLASSES of LendingPoint consumer-loan notes (May 2026), citing continued deterioration following a servicing-platform transfer that increased missed payments. LendingPoint had already lost Midland States Bancorp as a bank partner in 2024. Near-prime collateral (FICO ~620-659). MidCap Financial Investment Corp marked its LendingPoint loans at $40.2M vs a $63.2M cost as of late June 2026 (~36% markdown). Warburg Pincus holds a minority stake.
column6: ABS rating actions + a BDC markdown + a lost bank partner — three independent marks on one near-prime originator.
column7: Near-prime (620-659) borrowers are the cohort directly ABOVE the subprime tier CARL tracks; deterioration here is the K-shape middle giving way, not the bottom.
column8: HIGH — a 6-class ABS downgrade is a rating-agency verdict on realized collateral performance, not a forecast.
column9: KBRA (May 2026) via Asset Securitization Report / briefs.co 2026-08-13; MidCap Financial mark per same.
